messages:
jen: Quick RFC follow-up: we need a retire/GC story for on-prem artifact seeds + a stronger preflight semantics for airgapped installs. sketched a few options, want product + ops feedback before I bake it into the RFC.
rick: high level: we can't rely on long-lived global manifests in airgapped environments. operators want explicit retire semantics so old artifacts don't pile up.
maria: Agreed. Core requirements: (1) safe retire (no live rollback possible to retired seed unless explicit admin step), (2) offline preflight to validate signatures + disk space + compat, (3) deterministic GC policy that's reversible within a window.
sasha: idea: introduce three retire modes in the manifest: soft-retire (hidden from default UI but kept for rollback), hard-retire (eligible for GC after grace-period), and archived (immutable, requires manual recovery). each artifact has retire_ts and retire_mode fields.
jen: For preflight: support a manifest-only dry-run that verifies sigs, key expiry, minimal disk and memory footprint, and a compatibility check against local operator policies (e.g., max-model-size). This must work entirely offline once manifest and chunk hashes are present.
rick: operationally we should expose an "allowlist" and "quarantine" keyring: allowlist keys validate normal manifests; quarantine keys require explicit operator approval (useful for emergency fixes).
maria: How do we do rekeying? Enterprises with HSM/RSA might rotate keys. We need a rekey escrow flow that is airgap-friendly. Propose a rekey record in the manifest that includes previous key IDs + new key signature chain and optional operator-escrow blob.
sasha: rekey flow idea: manifest carries an array of trusted_keys with sigs; operator accepts new key when both old sig and new sig present OR when operator provides an admin-override token. For airgapped sites, escrow tokens are built as signed artifacts admin can import via USB.
jen: Garbage collection: propose a two-phase GC: mark-for-gc (agent marks eligible artifacts when hard-retire_ts + grace elapsed), then orphan-collect after a second window. operator UI lists items in mark-for-gc with a countdown and explicit purge button.
maria: safety net: once an artifact is mark-for-gc, keep metadata (small footprint) around for 30 days to allow manual restore. actual blob purge is the heavy op.
rick: what's the disk pressure behavior during installs? If GC runs concurrently with a large install it could cause eviction thrash. Need backpressure/lock semantics.
sasha: plan: installs acquire a per-storage lock and report estimated final size via preflight. GC uses lease tokens: if an install holds the lease, GC defers purge. Also GC should prefer deleting artifacts not referenced by any pinned deployments.
jen: test matrix I want: offline preflight success, offline preflight with missing chunks, rekey with mismatched old-key, admin-escrow restore, concurrent install+GC race, forced-purge when operator chooses.
deploy-bot: CI: queued job "airgap-retire-gc-scenarios" (expected runtime 38m).
maria: UX/API: operator should have endpoints: GET /artifacts (with retire_mode), POST /artifacts/:id/restore, POST /artifacts/:id/force-purge, GET /preflight?manifest=... returning {missing_chunks, sig_ok, disk_ok}. include compact logs for replicability.
rick: Security: manifests should carry sig_algorithm hints and a sig_ttl. If operator local clock skew is large, consider accepting server-signed timeproofs embedded in escrow blob.
sasha: implementation detail: prefer ed25519 primary, but support rsa and multiple sig entries. manifest JSON example in RFC draft: `{"artifact": "v1.2.3", "chunks": [...], "trusted_keys": [{"id":"k1","alg":"ed25519","sig":"..."}], "retire_mode":"soft-retire", "retire_ts":"1700000000"}`.
jen: Good. Also add a "retain_until" metadata field operators can set to pin artifacts from GC regardless of retire flags. useful for compliance.
maria: policy engine: allow admins to create auto-retire rules (e.g., retain 2 latest per model, retire older than 90 days). make this pluggable and visible to ops.
rick: logging: emit compact lifecycle events to the operator logs (artifact_id, event, actor, ts). Keep payload small so it can be shipped through constrained logging backends.
sasha: failure modes to document: partial purge (power loss mid-delete), metadata corruption, and misapplied retire flag. propose recoverable purge: delete blobs to a tombstone dir and unlink only after tombstone-commit window.
jen: integration notes: Console should surface artifacts eligible for hard-retire with an obvious "protect" button. default GC off for private installs until operator opts in.
maria: One more: offline-scan tool `redwood-artifact-check --manifest /mnt/usb/m.json --keyring /opt/keyring` that outputs JSON lines: missing_chunk, sig_status, recommended_action. We'll add that to docs.
deploy-bot: message: RFC update pushed at https://internal.redwood/rfcs/airgap-retire-gc-preflight, unit tests in CI.
rick: ok next steps: jen update RFC with retire-mode enum, GC lease semantics, preflight CLI output, and operator API surface. I'll coordinate tests with deploy-bot.
jen: thanks all. I'll post draft tonight and tag reviewers. :rocket:
